summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; no WebSearch used for 27C). 37 source leads recorded from the shared lead register and upstream findings (04B, 26D, 26A/26E, 18A/18D, 24C, 01B), plus leads marked 'URL from general knowledge - unverified' (India-Bhutan hydropower framework, Nam Theun 2 project page, UNCTAD WIR 2019 on SEZs, SEZ Authority Nepal, MIGA, IFC disclosures, CGD Global Skill Partnerships, PPI database, IEG). Q1 (which partnership structures have documented results in comparable economies) is set up as 10 hypothetical structure options: intergovernmental hydropower JV, export IPP under BOOT with guarantees, SEZ with anchor investor, FITTA technology licensing, training-plus-migration skills partnership, digital-services delivery centres, EPC-plus-finance under a G2G framework, development compact, DFI blended finance, and investment-treaty/facilitation upgrade. Each lists comparator cases to verify, Nepal's legal basis, feasibility conditions, trade-offs across objectives, links to 27A register rows and 04C conflict items, and scenario links. No documented result has been retrieved; all empirical items are pending and no numbers are recorded. The options are hypothetical and do not represent any government's position.

findings.claim: Q1: Partnership, investment, training and technology-transfer structures with documented results in comparable economies - 10 hypothetical structure options in specific.structure_options, each with comparator cases to verify, Nepal legal basis, feasibility conditions and trade-offs.
findings.period: case-specific; calendar vs local fiscal year recorded per case
findings.note: No case study retrieved in r1. Required per option: ex-post evaluation or completion report with outcome indicators.

findings.claim: Q1a: Current use of these structures in Nepal (FDI by sector/source, technology-transfer approvals, PDAs, IPP PPAs) as baseline.
findings.note: NRB FDI surveys, DoI approvals, IBN PDA list, NEA annual reports.

findings.claim: Q1b: Documented outcomes of Bhutan's intergovernmental hydropower model (fiscal revenue, public debt, diversification) as the closest structural comparator for SO-01.
findings.period: Bhutan FY (July-June) and calendar year as reported; record basis
findings.note: World Bank Bhutan CEM 2024 (lead 27C-L13); intergovernmental framework text (URL from general knowledge - unverified).

findings.claim: Method: only ex-post evaluations and official outcome statistics count as 'documented results'; ex-ante appraisals and commentary are context or locators.

Method: comparability is established by documented criteria (landlocked, LDC status, hydropower, remittance dependence, market size) applied to data, and differences from Nepal are stated for every case.

All structure options are hypothetical research constructs; none is attributed to, or claimed to reflect the intentions of, any government or company, and none is recommended before 27E audit and Agent 15/28 review.

data_gaps: Ex-post evaluations for each comparator case (Bhutan hydropower JV, Lao export IPP, SEZs in LDCs/landlocked economies, skills partnerships, EPC+F projects, compacts).
Nepal technology-transfer agreement approvals by year and sector (DoI) - no document-level lead.
IBN list of signed project development agreements with dates and structures.
SEZ Act/Authority records and zone performance in Nepal (URL from general knowledge).
Academic evidence on BIT/DTAA effects on FDI in LDCs - no document-level lead.
Comparator FDI series from UNCTADstat (calendar year) for the comparator set.

assumptions.text: Comparator economies are candidates to test against documented criteria; Bhutan and Lao PDR are named because of structural similarity (landlocked, hydropower export) and remain unverified comparators until data are retrieved.
Structure options are partner-neutral templates; any partner named appears only as a documented case, not as a proposed counterparty.
Trade-offs are reported across the 12 objectives (src/economic_model/welfare.py); no option is ranked on GDP alone.

challenges.text: SO-02, SO-09 and SO-10 depend on which BITs are in force (India-Nepal BIPPA contested); please resolve the status before 27E audits these options.

SO-07 (EPC plus finance) needs the financing modality (grant vs loan) of projects under the December 2024 BRI framework; 04B marks this pending - please retrieve MoF DCR/PDMO project-level terms in r2.
Add catalog ids for IEG, MIGA, IFC, PPI database, CGD Global Skill Partnerships and SEZ Authority Nepal; 27C leads use null ids.
SO-05 needs documented outcomes of Korea EPS and Japan SSW pathways for Nepali workers (placement, return, skills use); please include in 18D r2 if in scope.

uncertainty: Very high for r1: no case evidence retrieved. The evaluation literature on several structures (technology licensing, skills partnerships, BIT effects) is heterogeneous and may not isolate causal effects; comparability to Nepal (market size, peg to INR, transit dependence) will be imperfect for every case. Several leads are general-knowledge URLs that may not resolve.

structure_options.question: Q1 Which partnership structures have documented results in comparable economies?
structure_options.method: (1) Define comparator economies by documented criteria: landlocked, LDC or recently graduated, small open economy, hydropower-rich or remittance-dependent (criteria to be applied to data, not assumed). (2) For each structure option, retrieve ex-post evaluations (completion reports, IEG/independent evaluations, peer-reviewed studies); ex-ante appraisals are kept separate and never used as documented results. (3) Record outcomes per case with period basis (calendar year vs local fiscal year) and conflicts between sources. (4) Map each option to Nepal's legal basis and to 27A register rows and 04C conflict-map items. (5) 27E audits feasibility; trade-offs across the 12 objectives are reported, not optimised for GDP.
comparator_selection_criteria: LDC status or graduated within the past decade
evidence_hierarchy: ex-post evaluation by independent evaluator (IEG, ADB IED, peer-reviewed)

options.structure: Intergovernmental hydropower joint venture (G2G framework with bilateral off-take)
options.description: Two governments (or their utilities) co-own an export-oriented hydropower company under an intergovernmental framework; capital from grant/loan mix; power sold to the partner's market.
options.mechanism: Equity plus concessional finance under a treaty-level framework; off-take by partner utility.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: Bhutan-India hydropower model (Bhutan CEM 2024; intergovernmental framework text)
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: Mahakali Treaty/Pancheshwar Development Authority (27A AR-12); 2014 Power Trade Agreement (AR-05); PPP and Investment Act

documented_results.evidence_required: Revenue, debt and diversification outcomes of Bhutan's projects (tariffs, debt-to-GDP, construction delays) from the CEM and project records; calendar vs Bhutan FY basis recorded.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Partner-market access rules (Indian cross-border electricity instruments, 27A AR-08)
Debt sustainability of the equity/loan share (26A IMF DSA)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Export revenue and fiscal receipts vs public-debt exposure and single-buyer dependence
Environmental and resettlement impacts (welfare objectives)
Dutch-disease/real-exchange-rate effects documented in the Bhutan CEM - to verify
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.structure: Export-oriented IPP under BOOT with multilateral guarantees
options.description: Private developer builds, owns and operates a plant under a project development agreement, with political-risk or partial-risk guarantees from MIGA/IDA/ADB; long-term PPA with an export buyer.
options.mechanism: Limited-recourse project finance; PDA with host government; guarantees reduce sovereign/transfer risk.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: Lao PDR Nam Theun 2 (World Bank project documents and completion report)
Nepal's own Upper Trishuli-1 financing structure (26A AIIB lead) as domestic comparator
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: PPP and Investment Act 2019; FITTA 2019; NRB foreign loan bylaw; IBN PDA practice

documented_results.evidence_required: Completion-report outcomes (delivered energy vs design, revenue to government, safeguard compliance) for each case; PPI database transaction records.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Availability of a bankable export PPA under Indian approval rules
Contingent liabilities of the host government (PPA/termination payments)
Guarantee eligibility after LDC graduation and IDA terms changes (26C, 20C)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Foreign-investment inflow vs contingent fiscal liabilities
Local benefit sharing and environmental safeguards
Tariff levels paid by domestic consumers if export sales fall short
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.structure: Special economic zone with anchor-investor partnership
options.description: Zone developed or managed with a partner government/company; anchor investor commits to production and export targets in exchange for zone incentives and infrastructure.
options.mechanism: Incentive package plus infrastructure plus one-stop service; possibly partner-country zone developer.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: UNCTAD WIR 2019 SEZ case evidence (LDC and landlocked zones)
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: SEZ Act and SEZ Authority rules; FITTA; Industrial Enterprises Act (to locate)

documented_results.evidence_required: Zone-level occupancy, exports and employment for each case; Nepal SEZ performance records.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Transit time and cost to ports (21B, 04A Q3)
Rules of origin in Treaty of Trade and China LDC scheme (04C CM-02)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Export jobs vs fiscal cost of incentives
Labour standards and environmental compliance
Regional balance (zone location)
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.structure: Technology-licensing and know-how agreements under FITTA
options.description: Foreign firm licenses technology/brand/know-how to Nepali firms for royalty or fee, with training obligations; approval by the Department of Industry and foreign-exchange approval by NRB.
options.mechanism: Contractual transfer without equity; royalty repatriation.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: UNCTAD IPR implementation report (Nepal) as the domestic baseline; comparator evidence from academic literature (to locate)
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: FITTA 2019 technology-transfer chapter; NRB bylaw on royalty/fee payments

documented_results.evidence_required: Number and sectors of approved technology-transfer agreements (DoI records); evidence of productivity effects in comparable economies.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Approval time and fee ceilings in FITTA practice
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Productivity gains vs foreign-exchange outflows for royalties
Domestic firm upgrading vs dependence on licensors
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.description: Destination-country government or employers co-finance training in Nepal linked to a regulated labour pathway, with part of the trained cohort serving the domestic market.
options.mechanism: G2G MoU plus training provider plus skills test; returnee reintegration.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: Korea Employment Permit System (CGD Global Skill Partnerships record)
Other Global Skill Partnership pilots (CGD database)
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: Foreign Employment Act and DoFE rules (to locate); bilateral labour MoUs (27A AR-28)

documented_results.evidence_required: Documented outcomes (placement, earnings, return rates, domestic skills retention) for each partnership; DoFE yearly reports as Nepal baseline.

objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Remittance income vs domestic skills drain
Worker welfare and protection objectives
Gender inclusion
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.structure: Digital/IT-enabled services partnership (anchor buyer or delivery-centre model)
options.description: Foreign firm establishes a delivery centre or long-term sourcing contract in Nepal, combined with a skills programme and data/connectivity commitments.
options.mechanism: Services FDI or long-term outsourcing contract; export earnings via banking channel.
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: FITTA (IT sector), NRB rules on export-earnings repatriation, ICT policy

documented_results.evidence_required: Case-level employment and export outcomes; Nepal IT export records (08A).

objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Export earnings and youth jobs vs exposure to automation
Formalisation of freelancing income vs tax burden
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.structure: Engineering-procurement-construction plus financing (EPC+F) under a G2G framework
options.description: A partner government's policy bank finances a project built by its contractor under a bilateral framework; repayment by Nepal.
options.mechanism: Tied concessional/commercial loan; G2G project list.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: Comparator experience documented in IEG/academic evaluations (to locate); Nepal's own BRI framework modalities
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: BRI framework (27A AR-22); PDMO debt rules; Public Procurement Act (to locate)

documented_results.evidence_required: Loan terms, cost outcomes and completion records for comparable projects; MoF DCR and PDMO records.

objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Speed of infrastructure delivery vs debt and procurement risk
Local contractor participation
options.label: Hypothetical structure option for research; not a recommendation and not attributed to any government.

options.description: Large grant programme tied to agreed reforms and infrastructure (e.g. transmission, roads), with a local accountable entity.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: MCC Nepal Compact (27A AR-27); MCC evaluations in other compact countries (to locate)
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: Compact text and ratification record (27A AR-27)

documented_results.evidence_required: Compact evaluation results in comparable countries; Nepal compact implementation records.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Domestic political durability of compact commitments (no attribution of positions)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Grant-financed infrastructure vs conditionality burden
Timeliness

options.structure: Blended-finance and risk-sharing platform with DFIs (IFC/ADB private sector/AIIB)
options.description: DFIs co-invest equity/debt with private sponsors and provide first-loss or guarantee layers to crowd in commercial finance.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: IFC and MIGA project disclosures in Nepal and comparators
nepal_legal_basis_to_verify: FITTA; NRB bylaw on foreign loans; PPP Act

documented_results.evidence_required: Private capital mobilised per unit of DFI finance in comparable cases; Nepal DFI portfolio records.

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Currency risk under the NPR-INR peg (04A)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Mobilised private capital vs public risk-bearing
Transparency of subsidy element

options.structure: Investment-facilitation and treaty-based protection upgrade (BIT/DTAA renegotiation or new model)
options.description: Hypothetical update of investment-treaty network (newer model BITs, DTAAs) combined with investment-facilitation measures, as a partner-neutral structure.
comparable_economy_cases_to_verify: UNCTAD IIA reform cases; academic evidence on BIT effects in LDCs (to locate)

feasibility_conditions_to_test: Contested status of the India-Nepal BIPPA (27A AR-15)
objective_tradeoffs_to_assess: Investor certainty vs regulatory space (environment, labour)
Tax revenue vs attraction
